title: Choose the right playtest method
summary: Select methods from a concrete research question. Behaviour and opinion answer different questions; observations, interviews, analytics and surveys have different strengths. This informs the split between host observations and player impressions. It is games UX guidance, not a miniature-wargame balance standard.

title: Find usability issues in games with playtests
summary: Establish design intent, observe unexpected behaviour and ask neutral follow-ups. Teaching or intervention can change what a test measures. Usability problems and dislike are distinct. Applied here to setup, rule lookup and legal-action comprehension; severity categories below are Settlements planning choices.

title: Creating a Playtest Feedback Form for Your Board Game
summary: Describes internal, guided and blind playtesting; recommends concise, consistent, non-leading feedback questions. Does not prescribe a universal test-game count. Its pandemic-era platform discussion is historical; current community policies were checked separately.

title: The Conception of Viticulture: February 2012
summary: An early large blind-test shipment became inefficient when initial feedback immediately required revisions. Supports starting the unguided stage with one group, fixing blocking issues, then expanding. This is one designer's experience, not a controlled study.

title: Firefight Playtest Designer Notes: Part One
summary: Describes a small alpha group, public beta, version-controlled changes and remote play using Universal Battle. Importantly, online alpha play under-exercised climbing and elevated shooting. This is a concrete warning to retest 3D terrain physically; the 2021 invitation is historical.

title: Firefight Playtest: New rules and Asterians now available
summary: Shows public rules distribution, a dedicated feedback community and updated beta rules incorporating clarifications and adjustments. It demonstrates a workable publishing pattern; it does not establish that every community accepts unsolicited PDF links.

title: Providing Feedback on Prototypes: The WINQ
summary: Provides an original feedback framework and links to several other creators' evaluation forms. Useful for choosing a form style. Her page explicitly credits the original form authors; linked forms are reference material, not a licence to reproduce them here.

title: Game Salute Playtesting Feedback Form
owner: Game Salute; hosted by Kathleen Mercury
summary: Includes first/repeat-play context, memorable moments, strategy and rule-confusion prompts. It also asks commercial and demographic questions unnecessary for this early battle pass. Linked as an existing example; the new Settlements forms are original and shorter.

title: Capstone playtesting report template
owner: Educational resource hosted by Brian Schrank; credited excerpts from design texts
summary: Sets out observation and structured reporting as part of a playtest. Useful as a host/report reference, with an educational rather than miniature-wargame context. Do not mistake its academic framing for an industry certification checklist.

title: Playtest UK: free downloads and group information
summary: Lists separate designer and player feedback PDFs and explains its playtesting groups. The listing was read; the linked download endpoint could not be fetched. Marked listed-only rather than inspected. Old event dates are not recommended as upcoming sessions.

title: Weekly Online Playtesting
summary: Currently advertises free online sessions coordinated through Discord. Designers must use its roles and posting rules; listed platforms include Tabletopia, Tabletop Playground and Screentop.gg. Recheck the event roster and software before arranging a test.

title: FAQ
summary: Describes reciprocal playtesting, Discord coordination and supported virtual platforms. Its current FAQ explicitly excludes Tabletop Simulator. Use this to choose a compatible community; no endorsement of the FAQ's wider claims about a software vendor is inferred.

title: Steam Workshop
owner: Tabletop Simulator Knowledge Base / Berserk Games
summary: Documents custom mod distribution and public, friends-only and hidden visibility. Multiplayer assets must be available to other players. This supports a staged remote test build; a Workshop upload alone does not recruit testers or validate the rules.

title: Spam
summary: Prohibits repeated or unsolicited mass engagement and directs users to community-specific rules. A relevant, transparent test invitation is different from mass promotion, but permission varies by subreddit. The specific subreddit rule pages did not expose their full rules to this research tool.

title: Confidence intervals for proportions
summary: Provides the Wilson interval for a binary proportion. Used only for the explicitly illustrative independent win/loss calculation; repeated players, paired games, draws and multiple versions need different treatment or qualification. It does not specify how many game playtests are enough.
